- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (sentiment > 0.3) — reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment (sentiment < 0.1) — increase forecast lows by 2–5%.
- Avoid overreacting to recent spikes — cap forecast overshoots at +3% above immediate prior high.
- Apply mean reversion bias: if 3 consecutive forecast days exceed true outcome by >2%, adjust next forecast downward by 1–2%.
- For 30-day horizon, reduce forecast volatility when sentiment is flat (sentiment < 0.1 or > 0.9) — smooth out extremes.
- If sentiment turns negative after a spike, reduce forecast slope downward by 10–15% to avoid overcorrection.
- Forecast should not exceed 10% above or below 14-day moving average of true values unless sentiment strongly supports it.
